title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples

epigraph.quote: A control algorithm has zero value on a whiteboard; its worth is measured when it cranks a wet-magneto scooter silently in 45°C Delhi traffic or synchronizes a backup genset in 10 seconds flat.
epigraph.author: Operating lens on embedded mechatronics

web_blocks.html: SEDEMAC reports operations across two primary segments: Mobility and Industrial [4]. In FY26, Mobility generated ₹912 Cr (86.2% of ₹1,058 Cr total revenue), up from ₹564 Cr (85.7%) in FY25, while Industrial contributed ₹146 Cr (13.8%), up from ₹94 Cr (14.3%) [4]. However, H1 FY27 revealed a sharp segment divergence: Mobility surged over 52% YoY to ₹647.39 Cr (₹281.04 Cr in Q1 + ₹366.35 Cr in Q2), lifting Mobility to 91.1% of total H1 revenue (₹710.41 Cr), whereas Industrial contracted -21.8% YoY to ₹63.02 Cr (Q1 ₹28.73 Cr, -15.8% YoY; Q2 ₹34.29 Cr, -26.2% YoY) following FY26's CPCB IV+ transition surge. Beneath these two segments sit four distinct product families: (1) Sensorless ISG ECUs and combined ISG+EFI controllers (~60–64%+ of revenue), (2) standalone EFI and Aftertreatment Control Modules (ACMs), (3) EV Motor Control Units (MCUs, ~6% of 9M FY26 revenue) and traction motors, and (4) Industrial Genset AMF and engine EFI controllers [7, 8, 9, 13].

web_blocks.takeaway: Mobility expanded to 91.1% of H1 FY27 revenue (₹647.39 Cr) on record 1.45M Q2 ECU shipments, while Industrial gensets pulled back -21.8% YoY (₹63.02 Cr) after FY26's 55% CPCB IV+ surge—temporarily increasing Mobility concentration [4, 8, 13].

web_blocks.title: Concrete Example 1 — Mobility ICE: Wet-Magneto Sensorless ISG + EFI on a Mass-Market 2W
paragraphs: Customer & Problem: TVS Motor needed BS-VI compliance, silent starting, and idle start-stop on high-volume platforms like Jupiter, Ntorq, and XL100 [7, 15]. Conventional starter motors added weight, gear noise, and mechanical wear. Placing Hall-effect sensors inside hot, oil-immersed magnetos also posed reliability risks [7].

SEDEMAC Product & Integration: SEDEMAC supplies a combined ISG + EFI ECU powered by patented Sensorless Commutation (SLC) software (US12015315B2 / US12119769B2) [7, 10, 11]. At low RPM, the ECU injects current pulses and reads intra-PWM ripples in the stator windings [11]. This infers exact rotor position without physical sensors. It cranks the engine silently, then switches to battery-charging alternator mode and manages fuel injection [7, 15]. By September 2026, SEDEMAC crossed 1 million cumulative ISG+EFI ECUs within 23 months of launch, and by October 2026 surpassed 5 million cumulative scooter motor controllers (ISG + EV MCUs) [7].

web_blocks.title: Concrete Example 2 — Mobility EV: ISAAC Motor Control Unit & Logan Traction Systems
paragraphs: Customer & Problem: Indian electric two-wheeler and three-wheeler OEMs suffer field failures when water, dust, or heat degrades Hall-effect sensors inside traction motors [9]. They also face supply-chain exposure to Chinese rare-earth magnets [9].

SEDEMAC Product & Integration: SEDEMAC supplies its ISAAC sensorless Motor Control Units (MCUs) and Logan rare-earth-free motor platforms [9]. Running sensorless control in firmware eliminates the fragile motor-side sensor harness and cuts connector failures [9]. EV products scaled from 0.3% of mobility sales in FY24 to ~6% of revenue in 9M FY26 and continued ramping in H1 FY27, hedging long-term ICE-to-EV substitution [1, 5].

web_blocks.title: Concrete Example 3 — Industrial: GC500/GC800 AMF & CPCB IV+ EFI for Backup Gensets
paragraphs: Customer & Problem: Hospitals, offices, and telecom sites running diesel or gas generators (from Kirloskar, Mahindra Powerol, or Generac) need fast grid-failure detection and sub-10-second cranking [8, 13]. They also require true-RMS phase protection and strict CPCB IV+ emission compliance up to 8 cylinders [8].

SEDEMAC Product & Integration: SEDEMAC supplies panel-mounted GC500/GC800 AMF controllers alongside engine-mounted, IP67-rated EFI ECUs and electronic governors [8]. The AMF unit monitors utility voltage, commands transfer switching, and logs fault telemetry. Meanwhile, the EFI ECU meters air-fuel ratios in real time to meet CPCB IV+ limits [8]. After surging 55% YoY in FY26 to ₹146 Cr on CPCB IV+ adoption, however, Industrial revenue normalized downward by 21.8% YoY in H1 FY27 to ₹63.02 Cr (with Q2 segment profit down 33.9% YoY to ₹5.19 Cr), underscoring cyclicality in genset demand [4, 8].

web_blocks.html: A clear strategic thread links all three examples. SEDEMAC is extending its sensorless control stack into cordless power tools and smart FET voltage regulators [5, 9]. It is also preparing wet-magneto ISG kits, export 3-wheeler ISG ECUs, and a newly won European two/three-wheeler OEM ISG ECU and magneto kit program (start of production targeted for H1 FY28) [5]. Still, investors must weigh the current revenue reality: with Industrial contracting in H1 FY27, Mobility now generates 91.1% of revenue, and ISG-led ICE two-wheeler electronics remain the core cash engine while EV MCUs and European/non-TVS programs ramp [1, 13].

book_paragraphs: To see SEDEMAC clearly, strip away the buzzwords like 'deep-tech' and 'mechatronics' and look at the actual boxes rolling off its assembly lines in Pune. In FY26, SEDEMAC's ₹1,058 crore revenue came from two reporting segments: Mobility at ₹912 crore (86.2% of sales) and Industrial at ₹146 crore (13.8% of sales). By H1 FY27, that mix tilted even further toward vehicles: Mobility surged more than 52% year-on-year to ₹647.39 crore—91.1% of total H1 sales of ₹710.41 crore—while Industrial pulled back 21.8% year-on-year to ₹63.02 crore after FY26's CPCB IV+ compliance surge. Both segments rest on the exact same engineering foundation—embedded software that senses what a rotating machine is doing without needing fragile physical sensors bolted onto the shaft.
Let us walk through three concrete, real-world examples so you can picture how each segment works in the field.

Start with Mobility ICE, which is still the beating heart of the company—ISG and combined ISG+EFI controllers alone account for roughly 60% to 64% or more of total revenue. Picture an engineer at TVS Motor designing a mass-market scooter like the Jupiter or Ntorq, or a commuter workhorse like the XL100. When India mandated BS-VI emissions and OBD Stage II-B diagnostics, carburetors had to go, and riders increasingly expected silent, button-press starting plus idle start-stop at traffic lights. A conventional starter motor whirs loudly, chews up gears, and adds weight. Putting Hall-effect position sensors inside a wet, oil-splashed magneto invites warranty claims. SEDEMAC solves both headaches in one box: its combined ISG+EFI ECU uses patented Sensorless Commutation algorithms to pulse tiny currents into the stator windings, read the electrical ripples, and calculate the exact rotor angle in microseconds. Volume velocity confirms how sticky this architecture has become: SEDEMAC shipped a record 1.45 million control-intensive ECUs in Q2 FY27 alone (+37.5% YoY), crossed 1 million cumulative ISG+EFI units in September 2026 within 23 months of launch, and surpassed 5 million cumulative scooter motor controllers in October 2026.

Now shift to Mobility EV, SEDEMAC's bridge to an electrified future. Electric scooters and e-rickshaws suffer from a notorious field headache: water ingress during monsoons or thermal stress kills the Hall-effect sensors inside traction motors, stranding riders. SEDEMAC's ISAAC series Motor Control Units apply the same sensorless firmware to electric traction motors, while its Logan motor platform explores rare-earth-free designs that reduce dependence on Chinese permanent magnets. EV revenue scaled from just 0.3% of mobility in FY24 to roughly 6% of total revenue by 9M FY26 and continued ramping through H1 FY27 as OEMs qualified the units for production.

Finally, look at the Industrial segment, which requires a more nuanced lens after H1 FY27. Walk into the basement of an Indian hospital or a commercial office park and open the control panel of a Kirloskar or Mahindra Powerol backup generator—or look at small-engine gas gensets in North America built by Generac. Inside that panel sits a SEDEMAC GC500 or GC800 Automatic Mains Failure controller, commanding roughly 75% of the Indian AMF market and ~14% global genset controller share. Yet while Industrial surged 55% in FY26 to ₹146 crore on CPCB IV+ emission upgrades, H1 FY27 exposed its cyclicality: Industrial revenue fell 15.8% YoY in Q1 (₹28.73 crore) and 26.2% YoY in Q2 (₹34.29 crore), with Q2 segment profit sliding 33.9% YoY to ₹5.19 crore.

Across all three segments, the business model is identical: win a multi-year engineering design-in at the OEM drawing board, embed proprietary control firmware into the hardware, and ship millions of standardized, high-reliability control boxes over the life of the vehicle or generator platform.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The genius of SEDEMAC's combined ISG+EFI box is that it turns a regulatory cost (BS-VI fuel injection) and a consumer feature (silent start-stop) into a single BOM-saving architecture for the OEM. That is why adoption stuck—and why displacing SEDEMAC mid-platform is engineering-heavy.

book_subsections.title: Extending Sensorless Control Beyond Scooters: Power Tools, Voltage Regulators, and Export 3-Wheelers
paragraphs: If you stop at scooters and backup generators, you miss how horizontal SEDEMAC's core control stack really is. Any small rotating electric machine—whether it is a cordless drill, a saw, an electric three-wheeler, or a wet-magneto commuter motorcycle—faces the same physics problem: how do you know the rotor's exact position and speed without paying for fragile physical sensors? SEDEMAC has begun extending its sensorless commutation firmware into compact Motor Control Units for battery-powered power tools, smart FET-based single-phase and three-phase voltage regulators for two-wheelers, and Aftertreatment Control Modules (ACMs) for commercial emissions compliance.

On the November 2026 earnings call and H1 FY27 disclosures, management also laid out the next wave of commercial Mobility programs: full-scale ramp-ups of ISG ECUs for export three-wheelers, ISG ECU adoption on variant motorcycle models for top-tier domestic OEMs, a newly secured ISG ECU and magneto kit business win from a European two/three-wheeler OEM (with start of production expected in H1 FY28), and wet-magneto ISG kits targeted for commercial production in FY28. Still, you should keep the revenue math front and center: with Industrial softening in H1 FY27, Mobility now accounts for 91.1% of sales, and ISG-led two-wheeler electronics remain the primary engine paying for all future optionality.
